question.text: An oscillating <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>LC</mi><mo> </mo></math>circuit consists of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mH</mi></math> inductor and a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> capacitor. If the maximum charge to the capacitor is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The maximum current in the circuit will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_______</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi></math>.

solution.text:
When the capacitor is fully discharged, the current is maximum and all the energy resides in the inductor. Hence, the energy of the capacitor is equal to the energy of the inductor.

Li2m2=Q2m2C   ...(i)

 where im is the maximum current and Qm is the maximum charge.

The given values are 

Qm=2.7×10-6 CL=75×10-3 HC=1.2×10-6 F

The maximum current is found from equation (i)

im=1LCQm⇒im=2.7×10-675×10-3×1.2×10-6=9 mA
